proceduralStep.para: This procedure verifies the operational status and performance of the VHF radio communication system. Perform this test after maintenance, installation, or as part of scheduled functional checks.

proceduralStep.title: Pre-Test Configuration
proceduralStep.para: Configure the aircraft for the test:
Ensure aircraft main battery switch is ON.
Verify all circuit breakers for communications system are in (closed position).
Set VHF radio master switch to ON position.
Allow system warm-up time of minimum 2 minutes.

proceduralStep.title: VHF Transceiver Self-Test
proceduralStep.para: Execute built-in test (BIT) sequence:
Press and hold TEST button on VHF control head for 3 seconds.
Observe display sequences through all segment positions.
Expected result: All display segments illuminate in sequence, no error codes displayed.
Verify audio test tone is audible in headset or cockpit speaker.
Expected result: Clear 1 kHz test tone at nominal volume level.
Release TEST button. System returns to normal operational mode.

proceduralStep.title: Frequency Selection Test
proceduralStep.para: Verify frequency tuning and display functions:
Select frequency 118.000 MHz using control knobs or keypad.
Verify display shows "118.000" clearly without flickering.
Tune through full frequency range (118.000 to 136.975 MHz) using coarse and fine adjustment.
Verify each frequency increment responds correctly (25 kHz steps).
Test memory channel recall (if equipped) by storing and recalling test frequencies.

warning.para: Coordinate with Air Traffic Control or use authorized test frequency before transmitting. Unauthorized transmissions on operational frequencies are prohibited by regulations.

proceduralStep.para: Select authorized test frequency or coordinate with ATC for brief radio check.
Depress push-to-talk (PTT) button on control yoke or microphone.
Verify TX (transmit) indicator illuminates on VHF control head.
Speak test message: "Radio check, [callsign]".
Release PTT and listen for acknowledgment or request readability report.
Expected result: Acknowledgment received with readability rating "five by five" or equivalent.
Verify sidetone (own voice monitoring) is audible during transmission if sidetone feature is enabled.
Monitor active ATC frequency or ATIS (Automatic Terminal Information Service) broadcast.
Verify received audio is clear and intelligible.
Adjust volume control and verify audio level changes smoothly without distortion.
Test squelch function by rotating squelch control from minimum to maximum:
- Minimum squelch: Background noise audible between transmissions
- Maximum squelch: Only strong signals break squelch, weak signals suppressed
Using audio control panel, select VHF-1 radio for transmission.
Verify VHF-1 transmit indication on audio panel when PTT pressed.
Switch transmitter selection to VHF-2 (if dual radios installed).
Verify VHF-2 transmit indication and correct radio transmits.
Test simultaneous monitoring of both VHF receivers (if applicable).
Press emergency frequency button (if equipped).
Verify frequency automatically switches to 121.5 MHz (emergency frequency).
Monitor frequency for any active emergency traffic (do not transmit unless actual emergency).
Return to normal frequency by pressing emergency button again or selecting desired frequency.

proceduralStep.title: Performance Verification
proceduralStep.para: Verify system meets performance criteria:
Audio quality: Clear and intelligible with no distortion or excessive noise.
Frequency accuracy: Displayed frequency matches actual transmission/reception frequency (verify with ground station if available).
Response time: Frequency changes and mode selections occur within 1 second.
Transmit power: Adequate signal strength reported by receiving station (full quieting at normal distances).
If all tests pass, system is operational and ready for service.
Record test results in aircraft maintenance log with date, time, and technician signature.
If any test fails, refer to DMC-AMPEL360AT-A-23-10-00-00A-421A (Communications Fault Isolation Procedure) for troubleshooting.
Return aircraft systems to normal configuration.
